facts: The response of real GDP growth (q/q annualised) peaks at +0.303 percentage points, 1 quarter after the shock.
For a 0.280 pp policy-rate shock, the 68% pointwise band there is 0.145 to 0.502 and excludes zero.
Actual sample: 1999-Q3–2025-Q3; n = 105.
monetary_policy.equation: Yₜ = α + Σⱼ₌₁…2 Aⱼ Yₜ₋ⱼ + B Zₜ + δ′ Dₜ + uₜ
definitions: Y = (q/q annualised real GDP growth; q/q annualised CPI growth; unemployment rate; policy rate).
D = (COVID dummy 2020-Q1; COVID dummy 2020-Q2; COVID dummy 2020-Q3); exact indicators and coefficients remain in the original details and exports.
monetary_policy.settings: Vector autoregression · bootstrap · 68% pointwise bands · lags 2 · 1999-Q3–2025-Q3 · n = 105

facts: A one-percentage-point difference in y/y CPI inflation is associated with a 0.195 percentage-point difference in policy rate.
The 95% coefficient interval is -0.184 to 0.575 and includes zero.
Actual sample: 1999-Q1–2008-Q4; n = 40.
taylor_rule.equation: policy rateₜ = α + β1 y/y CPI growthₜ + β2 HP gap(log real GDP, λ=1600)ₜ + εₜ
taylor_rule.settings: Linear regression · HAC(4) · lags not applicable · 1999-Q1–2008-Q4 · n = 40

facts: A one-percentage-point difference in unemployment is associated with a -0.650 percentage-point difference in y/y CPI inflation.
The 95% coefficient interval is -1.12 to -0.179 and excludes zero.
Actual sample: 1999-Q1–2026-Q3; n = 111.
phillips_curve.equation: y/y CPI growthₜ = α + β1 unemployment rateₜ + εₜ
phillips_curve.settings: Linear regression · HAC(4) · lags not applicable · 1999-Q1–2026-Q3 · n = 111

facts: A one-percentage-point difference in y/y real GDP growth is associated with a -0.316 percentage-point difference in y/y change in unemployment.
The 95% coefficient interval is -0.587 to -0.0452 and excludes zero.
Actual sample: 1999-Q1–2026-Q2; n = 110.
okuns_law.equation: y/y change in unemployment rateₜ = α + β1 y/y real GDP growthₜ + εₜ
okuns_law.settings: Linear regression · HAC(4) · lags not applicable · 1999-Q1–2026-Q2 · n = 110

facts: Real GDP in Germany is 0.514% lower at the trough, 9 quarters after the shock.
For a 0.197 pp policy-rate shock, the 68% pointwise band there is -0.825 to -0.203 and excludes zero.
Actual sample: 2000-Q3–2023-Q2; n = 92.
same_ecb_shock.equation: 100 [log(real GDP)ₜ₊ₕ − log(real GDP)ₜ₋₁] = αₕ + θₕ identified ECB shockₜ + Σⱼ₌₁…3 Γₕ,ⱼ Xₜ₋ⱼ + γₕ′ Zₜ + δ′ COVIDₜ + s′ Sₜ + εₜ₊ₕ
definitions: X = (ECB DFR; 400 Δ log(real GDP); 400 Δ log(HICP); unemployment rate; identified ECB shock); 2 lags + one augmentation lag.
Z = (log(Brent oil price); y/y non-fuel commodity index growth).
A separate equation is estimated for each country and response; the same stage-1 ECB shock enters each equation. Other response equations remain in Details.
COVID indicators: 2020-Q1–2020-Q3; only active columns are retained.
S = (quarter 2 indicator; quarter 3 indicator; quarter 4 indicator); calendar seasonality controls, with the first period as reference.
same_ecb_shock.settings: Common-shock country comparison · HC1 · lags 2 · 2000-Q3–2023-Q2 · n = 92

facts: At 12 months, the cumulative CPI / cumulative NEER pass-through ratio is 0.747 for the same impulse.
The 68% interval is 0.650 to 0.845 and excludes zero.
tur_pass_through.equation: 100 [log(CPI)ₜ₊ₕ − log(CPI)ₜ₋₁] = αₕ + θₕ 100 Δ log(NEER)ₜ + Σⱼ₌₁…13 Γₕ,ⱼ Xₜ₋ⱼ + γₕ′ Zₜ + s′ Sₜ + εₜ₊ₕ
definitions: X = (100 Δ log(CPI); 100 Δ log(NEER)); 12 lags + one augmentation lag.
Z = (100 Δ log(Brent oil price); 100 Δ log(non-fuel commodity index)).
The headline ratio divides this cumulative CPI response by the cumulative NEER response to the same impulse, horizon by horizon.

S = (month 2 indicator; month 3 indicator; month 4 indicator; month 5 indicator; month 6 indicator; month 7 indicator; month 8 indicator; month 9 indicator; month 10 indicator; month 11 indicator; month 12 indicator); calendar seasonality controls, with the first period as reference.

facts: A one-percentage-point difference in the HP unemployment gap is associated with a -0.645 percentage-point difference in y/y HICP inflation.
The 95% coefficient interval is -1.04 to -0.250 and excludes zero.
Actual sample: 1999-Q1–2026-Q2; n = 1210 country-period observations.
ea_phillips_pooled.equation: y/y HICP growthₜ = αᵢ + β1 HP gap(unemployment rate, λ=1600)ₜ + β2 y/y Brent oil price growthₜ + εₜ
definitions: All variables and errors carry country index i; country intercepts are absorbed.
ea_phillips_pooled.settings: Panel fixed effects · Driscoll-Kraay · lags 0 · 1999-Q1–2026-Q2 · n = 1210

facts: Pooled HICP is 0.586% lower at the trough, 9 quarters after the shock.
For a 0.197 pp policy-rate shock, the 68% pointwise band there is -0.827 to -0.345 and excludes zero.
Actual sample: 2000-Q3–2021-Q2; n = 336 country-period observations.
same_ecb_shock_pooled.equation: 100 [log(HICP)ₜ₊ₕ − log(HICP)ₜ₋₁] = αᵢ,ₕ + θₕ identified ECB shockₜ + Σⱼ₌₁…3 Γₕ,ⱼ Xₜ₋ⱼ + γₕ′ Zₜ + δ′ COVIDₜ + s′ Sₜ + εₜ₊ₕ
definitions: X = (ECB DFR; 400 Δ log(real GDP); 400 Δ log(HICP); unemployment rate; identified ECB shock); 2 lags + one augmentation lag.
Z = (log(Brent oil price); y/y non-fuel commodity index growth).
Variables and errors carry country index i; the common shock has only a time index. The other response equation remains in Details.
COVID indicators: 2020-Q1–2020-Q3; only active columns are retained.
S = (quarter 2 indicator; quarter 3 indicator; quarter 4 indicator); calendar seasonality controls, with the first period as reference.
same_ecb_shock_pooled.settings: Panel local projections · Driscoll-Kraay · lags 2 · 2000-Q3–2021-Q2 · n = 336

facts: At one quarter ahead, ARIMA has the lowest reported RMSE, 0.550 percentage points, across 69 forecasts.
Its RMSE relative to the random walk is 0.736; this is pseudo-out-of-sample evaluation using final-vintage data.
Input sample: 1998-Q1–2026-Q2; n = 114; each forecast uses its own training prefix.
ea_inflation_horse_race.equation: ŷₜ₊ₕ|ₜ⁽ᵐ⁾ = fₘ(y/y HICP growth₁:ₜ, X₁:ₜ); m ∈ {Random walk, AR (BIC), ARIMA, BVAR}
definitions: y = y/y HICP growth; BVAR vector X = (y/y HICP growth; unemployment rate; 3-month rate; q/q annualised real GDP growth). Each model is fitted using only its origin's training prefix; this is a model comparison, not one pooled estimating equation.
ea_inflation_horse_race.settings: Expanding-window evaluation · paired loss comparisons; DM/HLN · lags 2 · 1998-Q1–2026-Q2 · n = 114
